title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy setting for profanity filtering in transcripts
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft has not identified an administrator role, but Microsoft documents meeting-policy management for Teams Administrator and Teams Communications Administrator. The filtering controls, default and rollout details are supported; the assurances about introducing no identity or permission need evidence or removal.

claims.claim: A Teams meeting policy controls profanity masking in live transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.claim: The filtering control also governs the saved meeting transcript.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: Filtering remains on by default, preserving the existing masking behaviour.
claims.quote: The setting will be on by default, preserving the current transcript-masking behavior unless an administrator changes the assigned policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Turning filtering off allows previously masked words to appear in live transcription.
claims.quote: When the setting is off, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in live transcription and in the saved transcript.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Turning filtering off allows previously masked words to appear in the saved transcript.
claims.quote: When the setting is off, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in live transcription and in the saved transcript.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The meeting organiser's assigned policy determines the meeting's filtering behaviour.
claims.quote: The meeting organizer's assigned policy determines the behavior for the meeting.

claims.claim: An organiser's filtering-off policy affects their scheduled meetings rather than requiring a separate choice for each meeting.
claims.quote: If an administrator turns filtering off for the policy assigned to a meeting organizer, words that would otherwise be masked can appear in both the live and saved transcript for that organizer's scheduled meetings.

claims.claim: The change adds no organiser-level control.
claims.quote: This change does not add an organizer-level control and does not change each participant's live-caption profanity preference.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Organisers and co-organisers receive no per-meeting filtering override.
claims.quote: Organizers and co-organizers do not receive a per-meeting override.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Live captions continue to follow each participant's existing profanity preference, unchanged by this policy.
claims.quote: while live captions continue to follow each participant's existing profanity setting.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: No administrative action is required to preserve current behaviour.
claims.quote: No action is required to preserve current behavior.

claims.claim: The filtering setting is in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting settings > Recording and transcription > Filter out profane words in live transcription.
claims.quote: A new Filter out profane words in live transcription setting will be available in the applicable Teams meeting policy under Meeting settings > Recording and transcription.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy accepts -Identity and -FilterProfanityInTranscript with Enabled or Disabled to control transcript filtering.
claims.quote:
Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity.
Possible values are:
- **Enabled**: Filters profanity from the meeting transcript.
- **Disabled**: Does not filter profanity from the meeting transcript.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference still says the feature is not fully released and the setting will have no effect.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription controls whether transcription is allowed.
claims.quote:
go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. Toggle **Transcription** **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription accepts $true or $false to allow or prohibit transcription.
claims.quote:
### -AllowTranscription
Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit.

claims.claim: The existing Transcription control governs allowing transcription, rather than choosing whether profane words are masked.
claims.quote:
### -AllowTranscription
Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings.
### -FilterProfanityInTranscript
Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity.

claims.claim: No admin UI or API controlling each participant's live-caption profanity preference is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams live captions profanity filter admin policy participant preference; "Teams" "profanity" "admin" "captions". Read meeting-transcription-captions and searched the full Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference for profanity; only transcript filtering is documented there.

claims.claim: No organiser-level or per-meeting override UI or API for transcript filtering is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "FilterProfanityInTranscript" "override". Read MC1478003, which explicitly denies organiser and co-organiser overrides; read the filtering parameter in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and meeting-transcription-captions. No separate override surfaced.

Read the record, MC1478003 and filtering reference; searched Teams Premium licensing for profanity/FilterProfanityInTranscript: no matches.

claims.claim: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.claim: The saved transcript is governed by the permissions of the file with which it is stored.
claims.quote: The captions and transcript file is stored with the video in OneDrive for Business or SharePoint. This inherits the same permissions and policy as the video file, so that whoever has access to the video file has access to the captions and transcript.
claims.fix: Add https://support.microsoft.com/office/3cb9acb6-05b2-4f59-a50d-7df61123aa20 to sources for the statement about transcript permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether downstream features such as Copilot recaps receive masked or unmasked text when filtering is off.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "profanity" "Copilot"; Teams live captions profanity filter admin policy participant preference per meeting override transcript Copilot. Read copilot-teams-transcription, MC1478003 and the filtering reference; no downstream masking rule was stated.

claims.claim: The change introduces no new identity.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "transcript" "profanity" "identity". Read MC1478003 and the filtering parameter in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; neither states that no new identity is introduced.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new identity or permission is introduced.' Keep the following sourced statement that filtering follows the organiser's assigned meeting policy.

claims.claim: The change introduces no new permission.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "transcript" "profanity" "permissions". Read MC1478003, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and using-admin-roles; they describe the setting and meeting-policy administration, but do not state that this change introduces no permission.
claims.fix: Remove the assurance that no permission is introduced; describe the documented Teams meeting-policy administrator roles instead, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Meeting policies can be assigned to specific users or groups using the steps on the transcription page.
claims.quote:
**To specific users**: Select your policy, select **Manage users** > **Assign users**
**To groups**: Select the **Group policy assignment** tab, select **Add**, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select **Apply**.

claims.where: Scope: Who configures it; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated which Teams administrator role can change this meeting-policy setting.
claims.quote:
Teams Administrator | Manage the Teams service
Everything in the Microsoft Teams admin center and associated PowerShell controls
Teams Communications Administrator | Manage calling and meetings features within the Teams service.
Manage meetings, including meeting policies
claims.fix: Replace the role gap with: 'Teams Administrator and Teams Communications Administrator can manage meeting policies in the Teams admin center and Teams PowerShell.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles and remove the role question from Open questions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Global meeting policy supplies the default for users without an existing policy assignment, while custom policies can be assigned to exceptions.
claims.quote: To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the **Global policy**. To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate tenant-wide master switch for transcript profanity filtering.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "profanity" "tenant" "policy"; "Teams" "transcript" "profanity" "master switch". Read MC1478003, meeting-transcription-captions and the filtering parameter in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; only the meeting-policy control surfaced.

claims.claim: The Learn pages do not yet describe the admin-centre location of the new filtering setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Filter out profane words in live transcription" "Meeting settings". Read meeting-transcription-captions, searched the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy text for profanity, and read the Teams admin release-note excerpt. No Learn navigation path for this setting surfaced.

claims.claim: MC1478003 asks administrators to notify compliance, legal and helpdesk teams before turning filtering off.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal transcript guidance if the organisation changes default policy behaviour.
